assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Heterozygous
items.clue: Having two different alleles of a gene, for example Tt.

items.label: Multiple alleles
items.clue: The existence of more than two alleles of a gene in a gene pool.

items.label: Diploid zygote
items.clue: The cell formed by the fusion of two haploid gametes at fertilization.

items.label: Recessive allele
items.clue: An allele that affects the phenotype only when it is present in the homozygous state.

questions.stem: A pea plant has the genotype Tt for the gene controlling stem height. Which statement about this plant is correct?

options.text: It has two separate genes controlling stem height, called T and t
It is heterozygous because its phenotype differs from both its parents
It is heterozygous, since it has two different alleles of one gene
It carries only the T allele in its body cells, with t only in its gametes

questions.explanation: T and t are two alleles, alternative forms of the one gene for stem height, occupying the same locus on the two homologous chromosomes. Having two different alleles is the definition of heterozygous.

questions.stem: Which list gives a human trait due to genotype only, then a trait due to environment only, then a trait due to interaction between genotype and environment, in that order?

options.text: Adult height; a facial scar; skin colour
ABO blood group; adult height; a facial scar
ABO blood group; skin colour; adult height
ABO blood group; a scar; adult height

questions.stem: A man and a woman are both unaffected carriers of the PKU allele. They already have one child with PKU. What is the probability that their next child will have PKU?
A woman with blood group A whose genotype is IAi has children with a man of blood group B whose genotype is IBi. Which blood groups are possible in their children, and with what probabilities?

options.text: Groups A, B and AB, each 1 in 3, but not group O, as neither parent is group O
Groups AB, A, B and O are all possible, each with a probability of 1 in 4
Groups A and AB only, each 1 in 2, because the IA allele is dominant to IB
Groups A and B only, each 1 in 2, since each parent passes on its own group's allele

questions.stem: In the four o'clock plant Mirabilis jalapa, a cross between a red-flowered plant and a white-flowered plant gives only pink-flowered offspring. Two of these pink plants are crossed. What phenotypes are expected in their offspring?

options.text: Pink only, because the red and white alleles have merged into a pink allele
Pink and white in a 3:1 ratio, because pink is dominant to white
Red, pink and white flowers in a 1:2:1 ratio, as both alleles persist
Flowers with red and white patches, because both alleles are expressed

questions.stem: Which statement about sex determination and the sex chromosomes in humans is correct?

options.text: The sex chromosome carried by the sperm determines the sex of the zygote, and the X chromosome carries far more genes than the Y
The sex chromosome carried by the egg determines the sex of the zygote, and the X chromosome carries far more genes than the Y does
The sex chromosome carried by the sperm determines the sex of the zygote, and the X and Y chromosomes carry the same genes
Both parents contribute equally to determining the sex of the zygote, and the Y chromosome carries far more genes than the X

questions.stem: A woman who is a carrier of haemophilia (XHXh) has children with a man who does not have haemophilia (XHY). Their first child is a boy. What is the probability that he has haemophilia?
questions.explanation: A son receives his Y chromosome from his father and his single X from his mother. The mother passes XH or Xh with equal probability, so half of sons on average are XhY and have haemophilia.

questions.stem: The heights in centimetres of nine students are: 150, 152, 152, 155, 158, 160, 163, 170 and 175. What are the mean, median and mode of these heights?

options.text: Mean 158 cm, median 159.4 cm, and mode 152 cm
Mean of 159.4 cm, median 152 cm, mode 158 cm
Mean 158.6 cm, with median 158 cm and mode 152 cm
Mean 159.4 cm, median 158 cm, mode 152 cm

questions.explanation: The nine values sum to 1435, and 1435 / 9 = 159.4 (to one decimal place). The values are already in order, so the median is the fifth value, 158. The only value that appears twice is 152, so it is the mode.

questions.stem: For a class's heights, the first quartile is 150 cm, the median is 158 cm, the third quartile is 166 cm, and the minimum and maximum are 130 cm and 192 cm. Above what height would a data point be categorized as an outlier on a box-and-whisker plot?

options.text: 190 cm
182 cm
174 cm
259 cm

questions.stem: Why is haemophilia far more common in males than in females?

options.text: The allele is carried on the Y chromosome, so that a father passes the condition directly to each one of his sons
Females who inherit the allele can only ever be carriers, because the female body cannot develop the condition
Males have one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele produces the condition, whereas a female needs two
The Y chromosome carries a second copy of the gene that is more often mutated than the copy on the X
